answer: A sybil tries to flood the agent economy with fake peers, but every new identity must lock a refundable bond that an established agent co-signs as voucher. If the newcomer cheats, both the deposit and the voucher's own stake get slashed. Spinning up a thousand umber shell accounts then costs real capital, and no honest agent will vouch without crystal-clear proof of past work. The cost stays as rigid as the fixed meter of a sonnet: each counterfeit line of identity demands its own locked payment.
